title: North Carolina's 6th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for North Carolina's 6th Congressional District pits first-term Republican incumbent Addison McDowell against Democratic challenger Cyril Jefferson, the mayor of High Point. The district was dramatically redrawn by the Republican-controlled legislature in October 2025, shifting from a competitive seat to one with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of R+9. Cook Political Report rates the general election as 'Solid Republican,' reflecting the district's new conservative tilt. The primary election occurred on March 3, 2026, with McDowell running unopposed on the Republican side and Jefferson winning a four-way Democratic primary with 39.2% of the vote.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in North Carolina's 6th Congressional District. Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid R.'

candidates.name: Addison McDowell
candidates.summary: Addison McDowell is the incumbent U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2024. A former lobbyist for Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina and former constituent services staffer for Senator Ted Budd and Representative Richard Hudson, McDowell has focused on border security, combating the fentanyl crisis, and supporting the America First agenda. He serves on the House Transportation and Infrastructure, Natural Resources, and Budget Committees.

candidates.name: Cyril Jefferson
candidates.summary: Cyril Jefferson is the mayor of High Point, North Carolina, and the Democratic nominee for the 6th Congressional District. First elected to the High Point City Council in 2019 and as mayor in 2023, he is the youngest person and first Black man elected to that office. A former teacher, youth development consultant, and founder of a social innovation firm, Jefferson's campaign focuses on affordability, healthcare, education, workforce development, and government accountability.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race, which caps confidence. However, the structural indicators are overwhelming: the district was redrawn in October 2025 by the Republican-controlled legislature from a competitive seat to one with a Cook PVI of R+9; Cook Political Report rates the race as 'Solid Republican'; McDowell is the first-term incumbent running unopposed in his primary; and Jefferson, though a credible mayor of High Point, won his primary with only 39.2% of the vote in a four-way race. The district's strong conservative lean, incumbency advantage, and absence of any countervailing evidence point to McDowell as an overwhelming favorite.
